questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 ?
questions.explain: Count the 2s: there are 5 of them, so this is 5 groups of 2, which is 5 × 2 = 10. Counting one group too many gives 6 × 2, which is 2 too much, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 2 × 2 or 6 × 5. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Siti works out 1143 + 4096 in columns. One column makes 13, so she writes 3 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.stemText: Siti works out 1143 + 4096 in columns. One column makes 13, so she writes 3 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 13 is the tens column: 4 + 9 = 13, and no other column reaches ten. 13 tens is 1 hundred and 3 tens, so the 3 stays in the tens column - worth 30 - and the small 1 goes above the hundreds column - worth 100. The small 1 is worth 100. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.explain: An even number ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, so the ones card must be 0 or 6. Try each one in the ones place, and each time make the smallest number you can from the other three cards. Xin Yi makes a pattern of figures with counters.
Figure 1: 5 counters
Figure 2: 12 counters
Figure 3: 19 counters
Figure 4: 26 counters
The pattern goes on in the same way. How many counters are there in Figure 12?

questions.stemText: Siti works out 2.74 + 5.7 . Siti writes the 7 underneath the 4 and gets 3.31 . What is the correct answer?
questions.explain: Line up the decimal POINTS, not the last digits. Write 2.74 and 5.7 one under the other with the points in a column, filling the short one out with a zero: 2.74 + 5.70 = 8.44. Writing the 7 under the 4 slides 5.7 one whole column to the right, and that is where 3.31 comes from.

questions.stem: A rectangular banner is 19 cm long and 10 cm wide. A notch 5 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 3 cm of edge before the notch and 11 cm after it, and the banner is still 8 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.stemText: A rectangular banner is 19 cm long and 10 cm wide. A notch 5 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 3 cm of edge before the notch and 11 cm after it, and the banner is still 8 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.explain: Walk the eight sides: 3 + 2 + 5 + 2 + 11 + 10 + 19 + 10 = 62 cm. Careful: this notch is in the middle of a side, not at a corner. The 5 cm taken out of the top edge is replaced by the 5 cm along the bottom of the notch, so that part of the walk is unchanged. But the two sides of the notch, 2 cm down and 2 cm back up, are brand new. Perimeter = 2 × (19 + 10) + 2 × 2 = 62 cm. A corner cut leaves the perimeter alone; a middle notch makes it longer.
